title: Seven objections to rewriting your C in Rust, answered in the order you raise them
subtitle: Each section is what a C developer says after hearing the answer to the last one. Seven objections at the top level, each answer provoking its own — read the top level alone and it is a complete short paper.
framing: **ver_E is a dialogue with a principled sceptic, and the ladder of objections IS the structure.** The reader is a senior C developer who has never written Rust, whose objections are principled — meaning objection N+1 is what they say *after* a satisfying answer to objection N — and who is open to evidence but tired of the pitch. Every section is titled with the objection in the reader's own voice; the answer is the evidence; the next section is what the reader says next. It exists as its own framing rather than a redraft of ver_D because **the organising principle changed, and that was the owner's four-times-repeated correction**: ver_A through ver_D were each organised by FINDING — a taxonomy, three chosen questions, an attribution thesis, four stories — and a finding carries no motivation, so every section had to argue for its own relevance before it could start, which is exactly the abstract opening the owner rejected four times. An objection carries its own motivation, because the reader supplied it. The order is the argument and is not rearrangeable: "the compiler can't always see it" exists because the previous answer was incomplete, `unsafe` exists because that answer introduced it, the proof exists because `unsafe` gave the safety back, and "why not just harden my C" is only sharp *after* all of it, where the honest tie on outcomes reads as a concession rather than a retreat. **The load-bearing node is the second one** — safe Rust is not C plus dynamic checks, proved on one program where the line-for-line port costs +69% and the tuned version +0.9%, same language, same pinned contract, same guarantee — which in ver_D was a supporting detail while the weakest finding led. **The construction rule, which is also the reading rule the owner asked for**: level 1 was written and read as a complete paper before any sub-objection existed, so any breadth-first cut of this document is self-contained; every paragraph must be traceable to the sentence above it that provoked it, and a paragraph that cannot be is a finding that wandered in from the data and is cut however good its number is. Kept from ver_D, which scored 8/10 against ver_C's 5: second person, contractions, short paragraphs, every term glossed as a trailing appositive in a sentence doing other work, one concrete subject at a time, each finding demonstrated exactly once, and every admission — asked which sentences bought the most trust, a cold reader named six and not one was a provenance claim.
